title: OBD System Readiness Not Complete
shortDescription: OBD emissions monitors have not finished their self-tests after a recent code clear or battery disconnect.
fullDescription:
P1000 on Peterbilt 579/567/389 trucks with PACCAR MX-11 or MX-13 engines indicates the OBD (On-Board Diagnostic) emissions readiness monitors have not yet completed their full cycle. This is a normal transient condition after an ECM reflash, battery disconnect, or bulk code clear.

The truck will not pass an OBD emissions inspection until all monitors set 'ready.' A full drive cycle — typically highway operation with varying load, a DEF regen, and cold-start to operating temperature — completes the cycle.

It is not a failure code, but persistent P1000 after multiple drive cycles indicates one of the monitors cannot complete (commonly SCR or EGR monitor blocked by another active fault).

causes.cause: Recent battery disconnect or code clear

fixSteps.title: Full drive cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Cold start, 30+ min highway at steady 55+ mph. Include at least one passive regen. Rescan after.

fixSteps.title: Check for blocking codes
fixSteps.instruction: If P1000 persists, check for other active codes preventing monitors from running. Fix blocking code first.

whenToCallPro: If persists after 3 full drive cycles with no other codes.

faq.a: No — it's a status code meaning monitors are still running.
Complete a full drive cycle. Cannot be 'cleared' manually.

title: DPF Inlet Pressure Sensor Voltage High
shortDescription: DPF inlet pressure sensor circuit voltage above normal — sensor or harness fault.
fullDescription:
SPN 3609 is the DPF inlet absolute pressure sensor. FMI 3 indicates signal voltage above the maximum threshold — typically an open ground, open signal wire, or failed sensor.

On Peterbilt 579/567 with PACCAR MX, this sensor is mounted on the DPF inlet and fed by a small sample tube. Vibration and heat cycling are hard on the sensor. A bad reading throws off the ECM's soot load calculation, which can trigger false regen requests or mis-detect DPF plugging.

Diagnose sensor harness first. Replacement sensor and sample tube is a straightforward repair.

fixSteps.title: Inspect sensor and tube
fixSteps.instruction: Locate sensor on DPF inlet. Check sample tube for cracks/disconnection. Inspect connector for corrosion.

fixSteps.title: Check circuit
fixSteps.instruction: Key on — back-probe reference (5V), ground, and signal. Replace sensor if reference and ground are good but signal high.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove old sensor, install new with correct torque, reconnect tube.

whenToCallPro: If wiring repair needed in harness.
videoSearchQuery: Peterbilt 579 PACCAR DPF inlet pressure sensor

faq.a: Sometimes — if ECM sees impossible values it sets derate.

title: Fuel Regen Dosing Valve Voltage High
shortDescription: Aftertreatment fuel dosing valve (7th injector) circuit voltage high — open or short.
fullDescription:
SPN 3480 FMI 3 on Peterbilt 579/567 refers to the aftertreatment fuel dosing (7th injector) valve that sprays diesel into the exhaust stream ahead of the DOC to elevate exhaust temperature for DPF regeneration.

FMI 3 indicates the ECM driver circuit voltage is above normal — typically an open circuit (broken wire, unplugged injector) or a shorted coil. Without dosing, active regens fail, DPF soot climbs, and the truck eventually derates.

Inspect the 7th injector harness, which runs near hot exhaust components — heat damage and chafing are common.

causes.cause: Chafed or melted harness near exhaust

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Follow 7th injector wiring from ECM to valve. Look for heat damage, chafing, melted insulation.

fixSteps.title: Measure coil resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect valve, measure resistance across pins — compare to OEM spec (typically 0.5-2Ω). Open = replace.

fixSteps.title: Replace injector/harness
fixSteps.instruction: Allow cool-down. Replace dosing injector with new o-rings. Use heat sleeve on harness during reinstall.

faq.a: Sprays fuel into exhaust to raise DOC temp for DPF regen.
Heat damage to harness and coking of tip.

title: Fuel Delivery Pressure Moderately Low
shortDescription: Low-pressure fuel supply below normal — plugged filter, weak lift pump, or air leak.
fullDescription:
SPN 94 monitors low-pressure (supply) fuel delivery to the high-pressure pump inlet. FMI 18 = moderately low. On Peterbilt 579/567 with PACCAR MX, the supply pressure should typically be 60-90 PSI.

Most common cause is a restricted secondary fuel filter — change per PACCAR service schedule (typically 50,000 miles). If filter is clean, inspect suction side for air leaks (fuel lines, separator o-rings) and the lift pump itself.

Insufficient supply causes HPFP cavitation, which can destroy the high-pressure pump and contaminate the common rail with metal particles — a $7,000+ failure chain.

causes.cause: Clogged fuel tank pickup or sock

fixSteps.title: Change fuel filters
fixSteps.instruction: Replace primary and secondary fuel filters with OEM or high-quality equivalent. Prime system.

fixSteps.title: Measure supply pressure
fixSteps.instruction: Install mechanical gauge at HPFP inlet. Verify 60-90 PSI at idle and under load.

fixSteps.title: Check for air leaks
fixSteps.instruction: Run clear tubing in-line at HPFP inlet briefly. Bubbles indicate suction air leak.

videoSearchQuery: Peterbilt 579 SPN 94 FMI 18 fuel supply pressure filter

faq.a: 50,000 miles per PACCAR, sooner in dirty fuel regions.
Could be a bad pressure sensor — check signal vs mechanical gauge.

title: Aftertreatment 1 Diesel Oxidation Catalyst Missing
shortDescription: DOC removed or severely degraded — temperature rise across DOC insufficient during regen.
fullDescription:
SPN 4752 FMI 7 means the ECM detected that during an active regen the exhaust temperature did not rise across the DOC (diesel oxidation catalyst) as expected. FMI 7 = 'not responding properly' — effectively a test-failure indication.

On Peterbilt 579/567, this can mean: physical DOC removed (EPA tampering, $5,000+ fine per violation), DOC substrate melted/cracked, or 7th injector not dosing correctly so DOC can't raise temp.

A factory DOC should raise temperature 200-400°F during regen. If monitor can't see this rise, EPA protocol requires the derate cascade.

causes.cause: DOC substrate melted from failed regen

fixSteps.title: Check companion codes
fixSteps.instruction: Look for SPN 3480 (dosing) or temp sensor codes — these are primary causes. Fix those first.

fixSteps.title: Inspect DOC
fixSteps.instruction: Visual check through inlet for intact substrate. Look for melting, cracking, or missing substrate.

fixSteps.title: Replace DOC if failed
fixSteps.instruction: Replace DOC assembly. OE DOC $2,500-$4,000. Reset adaptation in ESA.

whenToCallPro: Always — dealer or certified exhaust shop.

faq.q: Can I bypass the DOC check?
faq.a: EPA tampering — $5,000+ per violation, and truck becomes unsaleable.
Must be tested — ash-loaded or failed substrate won't pass ECM monitor.

title: VGT Turbo Actuator Voltage Low
shortDescription: Variable geometry turbo actuator circuit voltage below normal — shorted to ground or failed.
fullDescription:
SPN 641 controls the VGT (variable geometry turbo) actuator. FMI 4 indicates the ECM sees actuator voltage below minimum — typically a shorted wire, wet connector, or internal actuator failure.

Peterbilt 579/567 with PACCAR MX engines use a smart electronic VGT actuator with integrated position feedback. These actuators fail from heat exposure, vibration, and moisture ingress. A failed actuator eliminates boost control — truck may run in limp mode with no boost.

Actuator replacement requires recalibration with PACCAR ESA to teach vane position limits.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector
fixSteps.instruction: Check VGT connector for water, corrosion, melted pins. Clean with contact cleaner.

fixSteps.title: Measure harness
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect actuator and confirm no short to ground on harness side.

fixSteps.title: Replace actuator and calibrate
fixSteps.instruction: Replace VGT actuator. Run calibration routine in PACCAR ESA so ECM learns new vane limits.

whenToCallPro: If calibration fails or turbo shaft damaged.
videoSearchQuery: Peterbilt 579 VGT actuator SPN 641 replace calibrate

faq.q: Can I replace just the actuator?
faq.a: Yes — PACCAR MX VGT actuator is serviceable separately on most years.
Yes — PACCAR ESA required to teach vane endpoints.

title: Battery Voltage Low — Moderately Severe
shortDescription: System voltage below threshold while running — alternator, belt, or wiring.
fullDescription:
SPN 168 FMI 18 indicates system voltage has dropped below the acceptable threshold while the engine is running. On Peterbilt 579/567, common culprits include a loose alternator belt, corroded battery terminals, dying batteries, or a failed alternator.

Low voltage disrupts electronic controls and can cause cascading false codes on J1939. Fleets often find one dead battery in a 4-battery bank dragging the whole bank down — load test individually.

Never jump-start with reversed polarity — ECM damage ($3,500+) is a common consequence.

fixSteps.title: Check belt and terminals
fixSteps.instruction: Visually inspect alternator belt for glaze or cracks. Clean and tighten battery terminals.

fixSteps.title: Load test batteries
fixSteps.instruction: Individually load-test each battery. Replace any that fail.

fixSteps.title: Test alternator output
fixSteps.instruction: With engine running, voltage at batteries should be 13.8-14.4V. If low, replace alternator.

whenToCallPro: If alternator replacement requires belt/pulley service.
videoSearchQuery: Peterbilt 579 low voltage SPN 168 alternator test

faq.a: Best practice: replace all in a bank at once to keep age matched.

faq.q: Why do modules go crazy on low voltage?
faq.a: CAN bus and sensors need stable 12V+ to signal correctly.

title: EGR Position Sensor Voltage High
shortDescription: EGR valve position sensor signal above normal — sensor or circuit fault.
fullDescription:
SPN 27 monitors the EGR valve position feedback. FMI 3 = signal voltage above range. On Peterbilt PACCAR MX engines, position feedback is part of the integrated EGR actuator.

Typical causes: failed position sensor (internal to actuator), corrosion in the connector, or open signal wire. Replacing the actuator assembly is usually required since the sensor is not separately serviceable.

Heat and vibration at the EGR valve make it a high-wear item. Expected service life 300,000-500,000 miles.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug EGR actuator, inspect pins for corrosion. Clean if green/white deposits present.

fixSteps.title: Check signal circuit
fixSteps.instruction: Key on, measure signal wire voltage at actuator connector. Open = replace actuator.

fixSteps.title: Replace EGR actuator
fixSteps.instruction: Allow cooldown. Swap actuator, run calibration in ESA.

videoSearchQuery: Peterbilt 579 PACCAR EGR position sensor SPN 27

faq.a: Cleaning helps sooted valves but won't fix a bad position sensor.

title: Aftertreatment SCR Inducement — Final Stage
shortDescription: SCR inducement at maximum severity — 5 mph derate active.
fullDescription:
SPN 5246 FMI 0 is the final EPA-mandated inducement stage. All warnings have been ignored or root-cause unresolved: Peterbilt 579/567 enters 5 mph limp home.

As with all 5246 codes, it's a companion — the primary fault (SPN 3610 DEF empty, SPN 3364 DEF quality, SPN 4364 SCR efficiency, or SPN 4094 DEF pressure) must be resolved. Once primary is fixed, a drive cycle with ESA authorization will reset inducement.

Driving in 5 mph limp home extended distance risks tire damage, cooling issues, and traffic hazard on freeways — tow if possible.

causes.cause: Unresolved DEF empty or quality fault

fixSteps.title: Identify primary fault
fixSteps.instruction: Pull all codes with PACCAR ESA or JPro. Fix primary DEF/SCR issue.

fixSteps.title: Repair root cause
fixSteps.instruction: Address DEF refill, dosing, NOx sensor, or SCR issue per respective SPN procedure.

fixSteps.title: Clear inducement
fixSteps.instruction: After repair, ESA can force-reset inducement. Drive cycle normalizes status.

videoSearchQuery: Peterbilt 579 SPN 5246 FMI 0 5 mph derate inducement reset

faq.a: Limp is intentional — 5 mph only. Towing is safer.
Some repairs reset automatically. Others need ESA command at dealer.

title: Fuel Pump Pressurizing Actuator Not Responding
shortDescription: HPFP metering valve not responding correctly — pump or actuator fault.
fullDescription:
SPN 1347 FMI 7 means the ECM commanded high-pressure pump (HPFP) metering/pressurizing actuator to a certain position but the feedback (rail pressure) did not respond as expected. On Peterbilt 579/567 with PACCAR MX, this typically indicates an HPFP problem or a large rail leak.

WARNING: Common rail fuel operates at 30,000+ PSI. Never loosen any fuel line on a running engine. Wait 10+ minutes after shutdown before any rail work. Skin injection is a serious risk — see ER immediately if exposed.

Diagnosis requires rail return flow testing and metering valve current/response check. Often ends in HPFP replacement ($3,500-$5,000 with labor).

causes.cause: Low supply pressure to HPFP (check SPN 94)

fixSteps.title: Check supply pressure first
fixSteps.instruction: Verify fuel filter clean and supply pressure at HPFP inlet 60+ PSI. Starving supply is cheapest fix.

fixSteps.title: Return flow test
fixSteps.instruction: Measure injector return flow — a dumping injector starves rail. Dealer procedure.

fixSteps.title: HPFP replacement
fixSteps.instruction: Dealer job — swap HPFP, flush rail, possibly replace injectors if contaminated.

faq.a: Return flow test distinguishes — dealer required.
30,000 PSI diesel — skin injection is amputation risk. Respect wait times.

title: Outlet NOx Sensor Reading Below Expected
shortDescription: Outlet NOx sensor reading unusually low — sensor drift or plausibility fault.
fullDescription:
SPN 3226 FMI 18 indicates the downstream (post-SCR) NOx sensor reading is below plausible levels given engine load and inlet NOx. On Peterbilt 579/567, this usually points to sensor drift — NOx sensors have a 3-5 year typical service life.

Always replace NOx sensors in pairs if drift is confirmed — inlet and outlet age together and mismatched ages cause chasing faults. OEM PACCAR NOx sensors $600-$900 each.

Outlet NOx heat-soak from SCR is the primary wear factor. Sensor tip coking from excess soot also shifts readings.

fixSteps.title: Confirm with live data
fixSteps.instruction: With ESA, compare inlet vs outlet NOx at steady cruise. Outlet below 50 ppm at highway confirms drift.

fixSteps.title: Inspect upstream exhaust
fixSteps.instruction: Check all V-bands and exhaust seals upstream of outlet sensor. Leak dilutes sample.

fixSteps.title: Replace NOx sensor(s)
fixSteps.instruction: Use NOx/O2 socket (22mm). Torque to spec. Code may persist one drive cycle until learned.

whenToCallPro: If not comfortable working near hot exhaust.
videoSearchQuery: Peterbilt 579 outlet NOx sensor SPN 3226 replace

title: Engine ECM RAM Failure
shortDescription: Engine ECM internal RAM memory fault — reflash or module replacement.
fullDescription:
SPN 630 FMI 12 points to the engine ECM internal RAM (working memory). FMI 12 means bad or not responding — the module cannot reliably hold data during operation.

On Peterbilt 579/567, this is a dealer-level fault. An ECM reflash with the latest PACCAR calibration may recover the module; if not, ECM replacement is required ($3,000-$4,500 programmed).

Root causes include voltage spikes from welding without battery disconnect, lightning, jump-start polarity mistakes, and end-of-life failure. Always disconnect batteries before chassis welding to protect electronics.

fixSteps.title: Verify power/ground
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm ECM power and ground are within spec. Low voltage can provoke RAM faults.

fixSteps.title: Dealer reflash
fixSteps.instruction: PACCAR dealer attempts reflash with current cal. About 60% of 630/12 cases recover.

fixSteps.title: ECM replacement
fixSteps.instruction: If reflash fails, ECM replacement and full programming (VIN, parameters, injector trims).

faq.a: No — ECMs are VIN-locked and require dealer programming.
